name: The agents' workload: how much of the TC's evening they take
summary: On the evidence of the real page, the agents already do most of the work. One press on Name N shots runs the whole line by itself: Agent One names and grades, the room check follows, and Agent Two values. On 300 shots that took 1 confirm and 36 backend calls. A slow call or one answering only part of a batch picks up again by itself, and a person's typing is never redrawn away. The work that is left for the TC is in how the review ends, not in the naming. On a realistic 300-shot estate, 86 of 329 lines (26%) carry something a person must look at. Those signals are spread over a chip and three lists stacked above the rows, which push the first item down to 2,526 px on a laptop and 4,288 px on a phone. The only fast way to confirm the other 74% is a blind Mark reviewed that also ticks the flagged lines. The timing is wrong too: a tick made before Agent Two finishes is silently undone. The rows show nothing until each stage ends, and by my estimate from the logged probe timings a 300-shot house takes 40 to 45 minutes. That time is spent in an open browser tab, because nothing starts the agents except that press. Four defects let a wrong list reach the discerning reader. A 'nothing to list' line swept by Mark reviewed prints as a blank item on an Estate Inventory stamped REVIEWED. A too-dark photograph is labelled 'nothing to list' and advised for removal, and its Look-at-this note disappears with the line. 'Not duplicates' makes a line immune to every later duplicate finding, while the status line still says one was flagged. A room of more than 160 photographs is stamped checked although the server read only 160. Agent Two's 'Appraisal advised' and 'Worth a specialist' notes never reach the appraisal chip or the worklist, and they go quiet with the tick. The TC's own small name fixes are sent to full research and come back 'unsure' and unreviewed. Several sentences on screen still describe the pipeline as it was before 2026-10-25b. The plan, in order: fix the four accuracy defects; repaint by id with a 'valuing…' state per row; add a Look first / Ready to confirm pair of chips so the confident three quarters are confirmed in three presses; route Agent Two's advice into the appraisal list; start the agents without a press; and let Agent One suggest, for a one-press accept, the recipient and destination the crew said aloud.
works_well: The three stages run by themselves. One press on Name N shots (one confirm) named 300 shots, room-checked 6 rooms and valued 300 lines with no further press: 15 agentIdentify, 6 agentRoomCheck and 15 agentValue calls (s1_fullhouse.js).
When the server answers only part of a slice (its time budget), the run resumes by itself: 80 shots answered 12 of 20 per call were all named and valued in 7 naming calls (s4_failures.js D).
A naming call that fails part way still hands what it named to the room check and Agent Two: 40 named, 40 valued, and Name 40 shots offered for the rest (s4 A).
A redraw never lands under someone typing. After Agent Two answered, the redraw waited until focus left the row's boxes (s6_rename_research.js; step 107 D proves the same).
Agent One's empty answer is stamped and never sent again, so the Name button withdraws itself (s1: 25 'with nothing in frame', no Name button afterwards).
Mark reviewed's confirmation names what it swept past: lines that were unsure, the agents' notes and lines that left Possible duplicates, and it warns while Agent Two is still valuing (s2, s5).
The desk renders 325 lines in 98 ms and 650 lines in 594 ms, with zero page errors in every scenario run.
Agent Two never writes over a figure a person or an appraiser recorded, and a name a person typed is sent as checked and comes back as typed (s6 requests carry ':checked').
measurements: Full pipeline, 300 unnamed shots on a probate estate: 1 confirm, 15 agentIdentify calls of 20 shots, 6 agentRoomCheck calls (rooms of 50 and 25 photographs), 15 agentValue calls of 24 lines. 2.1 s on stubs. Measured by s1_fullhouse.js reading s.net.

Estimated real wall-clock for the same house: about 8-11 min naming, 6-8 min room check and about 26 min valuing, so 40-45 min in all. Reasoning, not observation: built from CLAUDE.md's logged probes (10 s per naming request, 27 s for an 8-photo room run, 62 s for a value call) and the server constants (AGENT_PARALLEL 8, AGENT_ROOM_PARALLEL 6, AGENT_VALUE_PARALLEL 8, AGENT_VALUE_TIME_BUDGET 120 s), with about 45% of lines researched.

Realistic 300-shot estate (s3_realistic.js, a stated plausible answer mix): 329 lines; 24 nothing to list; 38 unsure; 8 Agent One notes; 18 lines with Agent Two notes; 6 lines in Possible duplicates; 0 Needs appraiser. 86 lines (26%) carry a signal and 48 of them are outside the Unsure chip.

Height above the first row, after that run: the first row sits at page y=2,526 px at 1440x1000 and y=2,543 at 1024; the work bar is 1,101 px (Agent One notes 270 px, Agent Two notes 610 px) and Possible duplicates 376 px. At 390x844 the first row is at y=4,288 (work bar 1,759, duplicates 899). Measured by s3b_layout.js with getBoundingClientRect.

One press on a 650-line desk: a Reviewed tick takes 811-1,968 ms from click to paint, a selection tick 750-1,392 ms, and each runs one full renderInventoryTab of 189-573 ms. Measured by s7_tick_latency.js with requestAnimationFrame after the click; the machine was shared with other auditors' browsers.

Sweep-review of a 26-line estate: 3 presses (Not reviewed chip, Select all, Mark reviewed). Afterwards the Estate Inventory reads 'REVIEWED — all 26 items' while #8 and #20 print '—' (s5_empty_lines_print.js).
Mid-run, with the second call held: 19 lines named in the data and 0 shown on screen; the Unnamed shots chip still read 48. Valuing: 20 lines valued in the data and 0 on screen (s12_midrun_rows.js).
A one-word name fix on a reviewed everyday line: 1 extra agentValue request at research depth (mode comps, checked); the line came back unsure and unreviewed (s6).
verifier_note: On the evidence, the AGT report can be trusted on the facts. I reproduced every defect, inconsistency and accuracy claim myself, with my own stubs and fixtures, through the real controls (scripts in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-app/107e11dc-7b83-525c-829c-97f2e5cca8f9/scratchpad/audit/AGT-verify/). I also read the code behind each one. Where the report goes wrong, it is in three places. (1) Severity is inflated on AGT-02 and AGT-04. One case is a display contradiction whose removal still needs a press, beside a visible note. The other reopens a line by design: since 2026-10-25b the one tick covers the figure. (2) Some figures depend on the auditor's own fixture. The catalogue repeats the same names in the same rooms and puts a firearm on every twelfth shot, so the duplicate and notice counts, and the 2,526 px height, are inflated. The 40 to 45 minute timing is an estimate from logged probes, not a measurement. Separately, AGT-07's stub always answered research with no sold comparable, which gave it its 'unsure' result. (3) The auditor flagged none of the decided rules that AGT-07's proposal touches. AGT-16 and AGT-17 it flagged correctly. Every finding's description of today's behaviour checked out.

findings.title: Mark reviewed ticks 'nothing to list' lines, and the Estate Inventory prints them as blank items under REVIEWED
findings.jobs: all (worst on estate papers to counsel)
findings.where: Desk rows reading 'nothing to list'; the bulk bar's Mark reviewed; the Estate Inventory PDF. invLineReviewed (havellin.html:37222) does not ask for a name; _invBulkApply 'reviewed' (37298, stamp at ~37353); _invSetReviewed (37258); the row hint (39730); INV_WORK_FLAGS 'unnamed' (~37086); printEstateInventoryReport (31014) prints every _invAssignItemNos line.
findings.evidence: s5_empty_lines_print.js on a 24-shot probate. After the pipeline, Not reviewed chip, Select all and Mark reviewed (3 presses), the paper stamp reads 'REVIEWED — all 26 items' and item #8 prints '📦 8 — Dining Room 1 as photographed — not stated'. The same holds for #20. The chips still read 'Unnamed shots 2 | No value yet 2' with no Name button (agentNameableRefs skips agentConf 'none'). In s1 (300 shots) 25 such lines stayed in Unnamed, Not reviewed, Not yet decided and No value yet.
findings.tc_impact: TC: about 8% of a real house's photographs (drawer interiors, packaging) arrive as blank lines. They inflate four chips, and the only remedy the docs give is Remove line in each line's ▾, one at a time. Discerning reader: blank, unvalued items on a schedule that says every item was reviewed.
findings.proposal: Make a line with no name unreviewable. invLineReviewed answers false while objectName is blank. _invBulkApply('reviewed') skips unnamed lines and says so ('2 have no name: left'). The row box is disabled with a title. Give Agent One's status line one press: '24 with nothing in frame · Remove them' (invBulkRemove's writer over the agentConf 'none' lines, photographs kept, Removed items restoring them). Count those lines under their own chip, 'Nothing to list N', not under Unnamed shots. Have every paper skip, or mark '(not identified)', a line with no name.
findings.vnote: Own run, own Agent One stub: 18 shots on a probate estate, two drawers coming back empty and one too-dark frame. Three lines read 'nothing to list' (agentConf 'none'). Three presses (Not reviewed chip, Select all, Mark reviewed) ticked all 18. The Estate Inventory, from printEstateInventoryReport asHtml, is stamped 'REVIEWED — all 18 items' while #4, #10 and #15 print '— · 1 · as photographed · — · not stated'. Mark reviewed's message named only the note on #15, never the two blank lines. invLineReviewed (havellin.html:37222) never asks for a name, and _invBulkApply 'reviewed' stamps every line picked. The paper's claim is one the app did not witness. Minor correction: the bulk bar's Remove lines exists (Unnamed shots, Select all, Remove lines), so 'one at a time' is overstated. The concierge guide does say only 'Remove line in its ▾'.

findings.title: A photograph too dark to name is labelled 'nothing to list' and advised for removal; its note vanishes with the line
findings.where: Row hint 'nothing to list' (havellin.html:39730); agentApplyResult's empty branch stamps agentConf 'none' whatever notices came with it (37656, ~37680); invRemoveLine's confirm (29895); agentNoticesOn carries notes only from a removed photograph line to a derived line.
findings.evidence: s8_dark_frame.js. Agent One answers, as its prompt directs (main-sync.gs _agSystem: kind 'other' for 'a frame too dark or blurred to name'; 'Never guess at an object you cannot see'), with no objects and the note 'too dark to tell what is on the shelf: photograph it again'. The row then reads 'nothing to list', with the title 'found nothing (more) in it to put on the inventory… Remove line takes the line off'. The Name button is withdrawn. After Remove line, the note no longer appears in the list above the rows (listed: 0), and the confirm said nothing about it.
findings.tc_impact: TC: following the row's own advice removes something real. Discerning reader: an unidentified shelf of property silently leaves the inventory, and nothing anywhere asks for it to be photographed again.
findings.proposal: In agentApplyResult, an empty answer that carries an 'other' notice is stamped agentConf 'unread' (a new value; agentNameableRefs still skips it). The row reads 'could not be read: <the note>' in amber, with + Close-up and type-a-name as the remedies and no Remove advice. invRemoveLine's confirm names any live Agent One note on the line. Removed items keeps the note visible.
findings.vnote: Agent One's prompt does direct a 'too dark' frame to a kind 'other' notice and says 'Never guess at an object you cannot see' (main-sync.gs:3457, 3478). With an empty answer carrying that note, the row reads 'nothing to list'. Its title says Agent One found nothing, names 'a surface, packaging, or things that are not inventory', and offers Remove line. The note itself is listed above the rows and in the record. Remove line's confirm says nothing about the note. Afterwards the note is off the list (listed 0) and is kept only on the removed line's record. Rated medium, not high: the note sits in the record right beside the Remove button, and removal takes a deliberate press.

findings.fixed: 2026-10-27 (P8, its critical part: Not duplicates recorded for the pair, dupOKIn since its review (one id per press on every line of the group), agentDupCleared; the room check counts only a double the block shows; tests/p8-nothing-twice.test.js, browser step 121)
findings.title: 'Not duplicates' makes a line immune to every later duplicate finding, while the room-check line says one was flagged
findings.where: Possible duplicates block; agentNotDuplicate sets dupOK on every line of the group (havellin.html:38121); _arDupEligible (38082), _agDupEligible (37954) and agentNamedTwice (37970) all exclude any dupOK line; agentDuplicateGroups (38006).
findings.evidence: s11_dupok_immune.js. Day one: the room check links s0 and s6 (two sofas), and the TC presses Not duplicates. Day two: a new Living Room photograph, s12, named 'Tufted linen three-seat sofa', which the room check links to s0 ('The same sofa from two sides.', high). Result: s0.dupWith ['s12'] and s12.dupWith ['s0'], but agentDuplicateGroups is [], s12's row has no chip, and the work bar says 'Room check: 1 possible double flagged under Possible duplicates'. The same-name rule is also suppressed (same name, same room).
findings.tc_impact: TC: the status line promises a flag that is not on screen. Discerning reader: one sofa counted twice on the Court Inventory, because a different pair was once cleared.
findings.proposal: Record the clearance per pair. agentNotDuplicate writes dupOKWith: [the other ids in that group] on each line (on the manifest's save list and sticky like dupOK). The three eligibility tests then drop only a link between lines that cleared each other, so a new partner is still shown. _arStateHtml counts the doubles actually drawn.
findings.vnote: Own fixture, one Living Room. Day one: the room check links s0 and s2, and I pressed Not duplicates. Day two: a new Items photograph s6 arrives, and the room check links it to s0. Result: s0 {dupOK:1, dupWith:['s6']}, s6 {dupWith:['s0']}, agentDuplicateGroups [], no Possible duplicates block. Yet the work bar says 'Room check: 1 possible double flagged under Possible duplicates'. Cause: dupOK is per line (agentNotDuplicate, havellin.html:38121), and _arDupEligible, _agDupEligible and agentNamedTwice each drop any dupOK line.

findings.title: Review cannot safely start until Agent Two finishes: earlier ticks are undone silently, and rows stay blank mid-run
findings.where: _avWrite deletes valReviewed (havellin.html:38663), so invLineReviewed goes false; _invSetReviewed (37258) gives no warning; _agSendNext (37757) and _avSendNext (38946) repaint only the status lines (_agRepaint and _avRepaint), and the rows are drawn only at _agFinish and _avFinish.
findings.evidence: s2_review_during_run.js. With Agent Two held, the TC ticks s0's Reviewed box and Mark-reviews s1 and s2 (only the bulk bar warned). When Agent Two lands, all three show reviewed:true but lineReviewed:false, and s0's box re-renders unchecked. s12_midrun_rows.js: mid-naming, 19 lines are named in the data and 0 on screen; mid-valuing, 20 are valued in the data and 0 on screen. Estimated real duration for 300 shots is 40-45 min (see measurements).
findings.tc_impact: TC: the evening's review has to wait for the slowest agent, with blank rows and no time estimate. Any line ticked early must be found and ticked again, and nothing on the row says which.
findings.proposal: After each answered slice, repaint the changed rows, their group heads and the chip counts by id (the _invSplitRepaint pattern), when idle. Add a 'valuing…' badge on every row in st.ids, and hold that row's Reviewed box with the title 'Agent Two is still valuing this line'. On the status line, show '48 of 300 · about N min left' from the observed per-call time. Value room by room in walkthrough order, so a finished room can be reviewed while the next is valued.
findings.vnote: Mid-naming, with the second call held: 19 lines named in the data and 0 on screen, the status line 'Naming… 20 of 30'. _agSendNext, _avSendNext and _arSendNext repaint only their status lines; rows are drawn at the stage's finish. With Agent Two held, I ticked two rows' Reviewed boxes: no warning, no title on the box. Once the figures landed, both lines were lineReviewed:false and their boxes unchecked. The cause is _avWrite deleting valReviewed (havellin.html:38663). This is by design (the one tick covers the figure; Mark reviewed even warns), and the Not reviewed chip gathers the reopened lines, so nothing is lost but the press. Hence medium, not high. The 40 to 45 minute duration is the auditor's estimate, not a measurement.

findings.title: No way to confirm the confident lines in bulk: a quarter need thought, they are spread over four places, and Mark reviewed sweeps them all
findings.where: Needs you chips (INV_WORK_FLAGS, havellin.html:~37086, 'unsure' is invLineUnsure only); the Agent One and Agent Two notes lists and Possible duplicates above the rows; Mark reviewed (_invBulkApply 37298), whose same-name duplicate evidence (_agDupEligible requires !reviewed) is lost on a sweep.
findings.evidence: s3_realistic.js: 86 of 329 lines carry a signal (nothing to list 24, unsure 38, Agent One note 8, Agent Two note 18 lines, duplicate 6), and 48 of those are not under the Unsure chip. s5: one sweep of Mark reviewed said '24 left Possible duplicates with this tick … compare their photographs before you keep both', after the fact, and the same-name groups were gone. s2: 'Mark reviewed said: … 2 left Possible duplicates with this tick'.
findings.tc_impact: TC: the choice is 243 single ticks (about 1 s each, AGT-12) or a three-press sweep that also ticks the unsure, quiets the notes and erases the duplicate evidence. Discerning reader: a swept duplicate stays double-counted.
findings.proposal: Add two chips that read one predicate, lineNeedsLook(ref, job): the union of invLineUnsure, a live Agent One or Agent Two note, a possible duplicate, agentValueStale, specialist or appraisal advised, and nothing to list. 'Look first N' filters to them. 'Ready to confirm N' (not reviewed and not lineNeedsLook) lets Select all + Mark reviewed confirm the rest in 3 presses without touching a flagged line. Default the desk's sort within a room to Look-first lines on top. Optionally, Mark reviewed leaves Look-first lines unticked and names them rather than stamping and warning.
findings.decided_conflict: CLAUDE.md, Inventory: Mark reviewed 'still stamps every line it is given … a flag, every line stamped' (2026-10-26). The chips alone respect it; the optional skip would revisit it.
findings.vnote: The description of today's desk is accurate. The Unsure chip is invLineUnsure only (INV_WORK_FLAGS, havellin.html:37088). Lines carrying an Agent Two note under a confident figure, for example, are outside it: in v06_09, an $800 line with 'Appraisal advised' and high confidence was not unsure. The notes and Possible duplicates are separate blocks above the rows. Mark reviewed stamps every line picked, and same-name evidence ends with the tick, because _agDupEligible requires !reviewed. The 86/329 and 48-outside-Unsure figures come from the auditor's chosen mix. The proposed Look first / Ready to confirm chips are filters, which the decided rules allow (like Unsure). The optional part, Mark reviewed leaving Look-first lines unticked, revisits CLAUDE.md's 2026-10-26 rule that Mark reviewed is 'a flag, every line stamped'. The auditor noted that.

findings.title: Agent Two's 'Appraisal advised' and 'Worth a specialist' never reach the appraisal chip or the Worklist, and they go quiet with the tick
findings.jobs: estate (Needs appraiser) and living (To a specialist)
findings.where: agentValueNotices (havellin.html:39138) and _avNoticesHtml (39161) list them only while the figure is unreviewed; invNeedsAppraisal (27861) reads needsAppr, the threshold and valHigh, never valNotices; printAppraisalWorklist (35356) reads _apprGroups; on living work the 'worth a specialist' badge also goes on review (_avRowBadges).
findings.evidence: s3_realistic.js: the notes list reads 'Agent Two noted 18 lines to look at … Appraisal advised · If signed, this could be worth far more: have an appraiser look.', while the chips read 'Needs appraiser 0'. The Agent Two notice schema (main-sync.gs _avTool) has kinds appraiser, specialist and other. Mark reviewed's own message confirms that a note leaves the list with the tick ('now off the list (still in each record)').
findings.tc_impact: TC: reads the advice, then has to open each record and tick Needs Appraisal by hand, or lose it in a sweep. Discerning reader: an appraisal the valuer advised never happened, and nothing on the Worklist shows it was ever advised.
findings.proposal: Each appraiser or specialist notice carries one press, 'Add to appraisal list' ('Send to a specialist' on living work), which writes needsAppr as the person's edit (stamped by _invStampBy). Lines with such a notice that nobody has acted on count under the Needs appraiser / To a specialist chip as 'advised', and print on the Appraisal Worklist under 'Advised by Agent Two, not yet decided'. Mark reviewed's confirm says how many advised appraisals it is passing.
findings.vnote: Own run on a probate estate with values. Agent Two returned $800 ($600-$1,000) for a pencil-signed lithograph with an 'appraiser' notice. invNeedsAppraisal was false, the chip read 'Needs appraiser 0', the Appraisal Worklist (asHtml) does not carry the line, and agentValueNotices listed 's1:Appraisal advised'. After the row's Reviewed tick, the notice list was empty and needsAppr stayed unset. invNeedsAppraisal (havellin.html:27861) reads needsAppr, the threshold and valHigh, never valNotices. agentValueNotices drops notes once the figure is reviewed (39144). The proposal (one press writing needsAppr as the person's edit) respects the rule that Agent Two writes nothing a person owns.

findings.title: The TC's own small name fixes, and names typed onto blank lines, are sent to full research and come back 'unsure' and unreviewed
findings.where: agentValueAfterRename sets _avForceComps for any name change on a line with a stale agent figure, or with no figure (havellin.html:38921); agentValueMode (38465); server _avLineResult: 'if (mode === 'comps' && !soldKept) conf = 'low'' (main-sync.gs:4729); invLineUnsure flags any low agent figure (37245).
findings.evidence: s6_rename_research.js, with the stub following the server's rule. Adding ', gold rim' to a reviewed 'White porcelain dinner plates' line (General/Household, high) sent 's2:comps:checked'; the line came back conf low, unsure:true and lineReviewed:false. Typing 'Folded bath towels' onto a nothing-to-list line sent 's7:comps:photo:checked' and came back unsure. After the run the chips read 'Unsure 8' of 13 lines.
findings.tc_impact: TC: every correction to an everyday lot raises a flag the TC must clear again, on a line they just named themselves, plus a minute of research per line. Discerning reader: an everyday lot reads 'unsure' for no reason connected to its value.
findings.proposal: Send a rename at the line's own depth (agentValueMode without _avForceComps) unless the name gains a maker or brand (a capitalised word not in the old name), the line is intrinsic, or it is ticked for appraisal. The Restoration Hardware case still researches. Leave an everyday lot out of invLineUnsure when it is low only because research found no sale (have the server return lowWhy: 'no sold comparable').
findings.vnote: The facts reproduce. I added ', gold rim' to a reviewed General/Household plates line on a living job; it was sent as 's2:comps:checked' (agentValueAfterRename forces _avForceComps, havellin.html:38921) and came back lineReviewed:false. The 'unsure' half is only PLAUSIBLE. The auditor's stub always answered research with no sold comparable, so low was handed in. My stub returned a sold comparable, and the line came back medium and not unsure. The server rule does make a researched line with no sold comparable low (main-sync.gs:4729), and the 2026-10-26b own-page rule makes such comparables scarcer. The proposal narrows a rule recorded from Anthony (CLAUDE.md, Integrations, 2026-10-25b: 'A name changed is valued again by itself … researched (_avForceComps)', and 'a figure accepted for the old name is accepted no longer'). It also touches AGENT_TWO_SPEC §4b (research with no sold comparable is low). Ask Anthony; do not build it silently.

findings.title: A room of more than 160 photographs is stamped 'checked' although the server read only the first 160
findings.jobs: all (big garages, kitchens photographed drawer by drawer)
findings.where: Server agentCheckRooms: 'var shots = ((room && room.shots) || []).slice(0, AGENT_ROOM_MAX_SHOTS)' (main-sync.gs:3994), answered with photos: st.shots.length; app _arWrite stamps dupChkAt on every line the room sent (havellin.html:38332) and never reads result.photos; _arSendNext (38278).
findings.evidence: s10_room_cap.js, a 200-shot Garage, with the stub answering as the server does (photos: 160): 183 photographs sent, 199 checkable lines and 199 stamped; agentRoomsToCheck → 0 rooms; the status line reads 'nothing photographed twice in the 1 room read'.
findings.tc_impact: TC: 'nothing photographed twice' is shown for photographs nobody compared, and Check N rooms never comes back for them. Discerning reader: doubles among the last photographs of a large room go uncaught.
findings.proposal: _arWrite stamps only the lines from the first result.photos photographs (in the order sent); the rest stay fresh, so the next call carries them with an overlap of AGENT_ROOM_OVERLAP. Alternatively, _arSendNext splits a room over 160 into overlapping chunks of 160 itself.
findings.vnote: The server slices each room to AGENT_ROOM_MAX_SHOTS = 160 (main-sync.gs:3994) and answers photos: st.shots.length. The app never reads 'photos'; _arWrite stamps dupChkAt on every line it sent. Own run: 600 shots in two rooms, 300 and 250 photographs sent. All 600 checkable lines were stamped, agentRoomsToCheck returned 0, and the status line read 'nothing photographed twice in the 2 rooms read'. Rated low: more than 160 Items photographs in one room is rare.

findings.title: Sentences beside the agents' buttons still describe the old pipeline (siblings of the stale Name N shots confirm)
findings.where: agentValueRun's confirm (havellin.html:38810, 38812) and its 'nothing to value' alert; agentRoomCheckRun's confirm (~38264); the Name button's title (39376).
findings.evidence: s9_dialog_words.js, pressing the real buttons. Value 24 lines says 'Nothing else on the line changes', but _avWrite grades condition (_invAgentCondition) and can move a research line's category (s9 'after': 24 lines graded by Agent Two). It also says '2 unnamed lines are left out: name them first', where both lines are nothing-to-list photographs that Name shots will never send. The Check 6 rooms confirm says nothing of valuing, yet Agent Two ran by itself after it (2 agentValue calls). The Name button's title reads 'fill in a name and a category' and omits the count and the condition.
findings.tc_impact: TC: the words on screen promise less than the agents then do, and the remedy they give ('name them first') is a dead end.
findings.proposal: Value N lines: 'Agent Two may also correct the category of a researched line and grades condition off the photograph; nothing you set is changed.' Leave nothing-to-list lines out of 'unnamed', or call them 'photographs with nothing to list (Remove lines)'. Check N rooms: '…then Agent Two values the lines by itself.' Name button title: 'a name, a category, a count and a condition'. Fix the Name confirm as the planner found.
findings.vnote: Pressing the real Value 4 lines button gave a confirm that reads '… Each line’s Reviewed tick covers its value too. Nothing else on the line changes. 2 unnamed lines are left out: name them first.' Afterwards all four lines had condition 'Fair' with condBy 'agent' (_avWrite → _invAgentCondition). _avWrite can also move the category of an Agent One-named research line (havellin.html:38658). The two 'unnamed' lines were both nothing-to-list lines, which Name shots never sends, so 'name them first' is a dead end. Read in the code: Check N rooms' confirm says nothing about Agent Two following (_arFinish → agentValueAuto). The Name button's title says 'a name and a category' and leaves out the count and the condition, though it does say the values follow.

findings.title: The agents run only from one press in an open desk tab, one call at a time; nothing starts them as the field uploads
findings.where: The only caller of agentNameShots is the work bar's button (havellin.html:39375); _agFinish → agentRoomCheckRun → _arFinish → agentValueAuto run in the page session; AGENT_BATCH 20 (37516) against the server's AGENT_MAX_SHOTS 80; AGENT_VALUE_BATCH 24 against 40; each stage sends its next call only after the last answers.
findings.evidence: grep: agentNameShots( is called only from the button markup. s1: 15 sequential naming calls of 20 for 300 shots. The 40-45 min estimate (measurements) is spent with the tab open; a closed laptop or a sleeping iPad stops the run (reasoning: session-only state in _agState and _avState), and only the Name, Check and Value buttons are left to restart it.
findings.tc_impact: TC: the evening opens with a press and then a long wait in front of blank rows, where the agents could have worked through the afternoon's uploads.
findings.proposal: Start the pipeline without a confirm when the desk opens on a client with nameable shots in Drive, and when the camera's Done is pressed online, saying so on the status line. Send 80 shots per naming call. Run two Agent Two calls at once (the queue is by id, so they cannot overlap). Longer term, a server-side time-driven pass over new Items shots writing through the same merge rules.
findings.vnote: agentNameShots( has one caller, the work bar's button (havellin.html:39375). The whole chain runs in page session state (_agState, _avState, _arState). Batches are AGENT_BATCH 20 against the server's 80, and AGENT_VALUE_BATCH 24 against its 40, sent one call at a time. The timing is the auditor's reasoning, not a measurement. The proposal conflicts with no decided rule. One risk it does not mention: auto-starting on desk open on two devices at once would aggravate the known two-device double Agent Two run (Known, 2026-10-25b) and produce 'one photograph named twice' groups.

findings.title: The notes lists and Possible duplicates push the first item to 2.5 screens down on a laptop and 5 on a phone
findings.where: _agNoticesHtml (havellin.html:39477, uncapped), _avNoticesHtml (39161, 12 lines drawn), _agDupHtml (38138, 8 groups), all above the rows in the work bar and the filter area.
findings.evidence: s3b_layout.js after the realistic 300-shot run: first row at y=2,526 (1440), 2,543 (1024) and 4,288 (390x844); work bar 1,101 px, of which Agent One notes are 270 and Agent Two notes 610; duplicates 376 (899 on a phone). s1: Agent One's list drew all 25 firearm notices.
findings.tc_impact: TC: scrolls past a wall of prose to reach any item and back up to act on a note; on the iPad in the house this is the whole screen.
findings.proposal: Collapse each list to one line per kind with a count and a filter: 'Firearm 2 · Look at this 6 · Appraisal advised 9 · Possible duplicates 3 groups'. Each opens the matching rows (the Look first chip of AGT-05) and keeps Show the item. Keep Firearm and NFA always drawn, in red, as one line with the count. Show the first duplicate group expanded and the rest as 'N more'.
findings.vnote: _agNoticesHtml (havellin.html:39477) draws every notice, uncapped. _avNoticesHtml draws 12 lines and _agDupHtml 8 groups, all above the rows. The auditor's 2,526 px also comes from a chosen mix. The pattern is real; the exact heights are not representative. The proposal keeps Firearm and NFA drawn in red, so it fits Q90.

findings.title: Every Reviewed tick and every selection tick redraws the whole desk: 0.8–2 s a press on a full house
findings.evidence: s7_tick_latency.js at 650 lines: Reviewed tick click-to-paint 1,968, 811, 933, 1,417 and 1,866 ms; selection tick 1,392, 1,027, 798, 750 and 871 ms; 10 presses ran 10 full renders of 189-573 ms each (machine shared with other auditors).
findings.tc_impact: TC: the one-look model is one tick per line, so 300-600 ticks cost minutes of waiting. Selecting 40 lines one by one is 40 full redraws.
findings.proposal: Repaint by id: the row, its group's 'N of M reviewed', the progress bar and the chip counts for a tick; the row's background and the bulk bar for a selection. Fall back to renderInventoryTab only where a row cannot be placed (the _invSplitRepaint pattern, with a byte-for-byte test against the full render).
findings.vnote: _invSetReviewed (havellin.html:37267) and _invTogglePick (37279) each end in renderInventoryTab. On 650 lines, measured in the page (pointerdown to the second animation frame), a Reviewed tick took 572-909 ms and a selection tick 650-679 ms. One full renderInventoryTab was 191-241 ms of that; the rest is savePhotoRefs and paint. The machine was shared with other browsers, so the absolute figures are approximate. The auditor's 0.8-2 s is the upper end, measured with Playwright overhead included.

findings.title: A failed room check leaves Agent Two unstarted with nothing saying the values are waiting; error lines carry raw exceptions and no next press
findings.where: _arFinish: 'if (!st.error) agentValueAuto(jobId)' (havellin.html:38362); _arStateHtml (38379); _agStateHtml (37823) shows only the error once st.error is set; _avStateHtml (39053).
findings.evidence: s4_failures.js. B: the room check answers ok:false. The line reads '⚠ Room check: Exception: Timeout: https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages', the value line is empty, 0 of 79 lines are valued, and the bar shows 'Check 6 rooms | Value 79 lines'. A: the naming line reads only '⚠ Exception: Service invoked too many times for one day: urlfetch.' and hides that 40 were named. C: '⚠ Agent Two: Failed to fetch' with 59 lines unvalued.
findings.tc_impact: TC: no values appear, and the screen does not say which press brings them; a quota error reads like a crash.
findings.proposal: Start Agent Two even after a failed check: a repeat is still flagged later, and removing it takes its value with it, as the manual already says. Otherwise the room line should say 'Agent Two waits: press Check 6 rooms again, or Value 79 lines'. Map errors to plain words with the next press (the _agFailureKind pattern): 'the day's quota is used up: try again tomorrow', 'could not reach the service: press Value 59 lines'. Keep the counts beside the error.
findings.vnote: The room check answered ok:false, as agentCheckRooms' catch returns String(error), with a quota error. The line read '⚠ Room check: Exception: Service invoked too many times for one day: urlfetch.'; the value line was empty; 0 agentValue calls; Check 2 rooms and Value 12 lines were offered with no sentence saying which to press. _arFinish skips Agent Two on error by design (code comment: 'a line counted twice is a line valued twice'), while _agFinish does hand on after a part-failed naming run. The first option in the proposal (start Agent Two anyway) revisits that recorded choice; the second (say which press brings the values) is clean. Low: the buttons are on screen.

findings.title: Who it goes to, said at the camera ('going to Karen'), stays in the note; the TC re-types every recipient
findings.where: photography-guide.html has the crew say 'Mom's, from Venice, going to Karen'. Agent One reads the note and is told to keep recipients out of the name (main-sync.gs _agSystem 'THE NOTES WITH A PHOTOGRAPH', 3418). The record_contents schema (_agTool, 3266) has no field for it, and the desk's 'Who takes it' (_invRecipientInput) and the No recipient chip are filled only by hand or by a confirmed vendor (invFillPlanChannel).
findings.evidence: Code reading: no reader parses fieldNote for a recipient or a destination. The row shows the note as text only (havellin.html:39797).
findings.tc_impact: TC: on an estate every To-a-person line needs a recipient before the release request carries it (lines with nobody named are held off), so each spoken name is typed again. Discerning reader: a recipient typed from memory is a recipient mistyped.
findings.proposal: Agent One returns saidTo (a person or charity named in the crew's note, verbatim) and saidDest (keep / new home / donate / sell / remove, where the note says one). The row shows 'Note says: to Karen · Use', and one press writes channel (and the disposition, if it is still Undecided) as the person's edit. Nothing is written without the press.
findings.decided_conflict: Decided: 'Agent One writing a value, a disposition or an NFA flag'. This is a suggestion the TC accepts with a press; the agent writes nothing.
findings.vnote: photography-guide.html:405 has the crew say 'Mom’s, from Venice, going to Karen'. Agent One's prompt keeps recipients out of the name (main-sync.gs:3418-3424). The record_contents schema has no recipient field, and nothing in the app reads fieldNote into channel (grep: fieldNote is read only by search, havellin.html:37141). As a one-press suggestion of the recipient, the proposal stays within 'Agent One writing a value, a disposition or an NFA flag'. Its saidDest part sits closer to that rule, and to Agent One's own prompt ('Never say what should happen to an object'). The field chips already record the destination, so recipient-only is the clean version.
findings.vrepro: photography-guide.html:405; main-sync.gs:3418-3424 and _agTool (no recipient field); grep -n 'saidTo\|fieldNote' havellin.html

findings.title: A must-find sighting cannot be recorded from the notice that reports it
findings.where: The notices schema is {kind, text} only (main-sync.gs _agTool); agentNoticeQuiet's mustfind arm waits for mustFindAllFound (havellin.html:37868, comment: 'a notice carries no must-find key'); _agNoticesHtml offers only Show the item.
findings.evidence: Code reading. The must-find tick is in the must-finds block at the top of the desk (sf-host-desk), a separate place from the notice.
findings.tc_impact: TC: reads 'Must find · Primary Bedroom · #41 — a strongbox …', scrolls up to the must-finds, works out which one it was and ticks it; the red notice stays until every must-find is found.
findings.proposal: Add 'which' to the mustfind notice (an enum of ctx.mustFind) and a 'Found it' button on the notice that writes the existing must-find tick as the person's act (who and when), after a confirm naming the item and the line. Quiet that notice once its own must-find is found.
findings.vnote: The notice schema is {kind, text} with kind in mustfind/firearm/nfa/other (main-sync.gs _agTool). The mustfind arm of agentNoticeQuiet waits on mustFindAllFound (havellin.html:37868). The notice offers only Show the item. The 'Found it' button is allowed. Quieting each notice on its own must-find refines Q90's chosen wording ('a must-find note goes quiet once every must-find is found'); confirm that with Anthony.

findings.title: Nothing checks the inventory against the as-found photographs, so a thing never given an Items shot is never caught
findings.where: agentShotGroups sends only Items shots; the room check reads Items photographs only (agentRoomsToCheck); the as-found pass is evidence only.
findings.evidence: Code reading and Decided. The guide's own failure case ('dresser, vase, vase') shows the crew can miss or double things; the room check catches the doubles, and nothing catches the misses. Reasoning, not observation.
findings.tc_impact: TC: completeness rests on the crew's discipline alone. Discerning reader: the bar is 'complete, nothing missed', and an omitted grandfather clock seen in the as-found photograph is exactly what an attorney's own walk-through finds.
findings.proposal: An optional, flag-only 'As-found check' per room, run after the room check: the room's as-found photographs plus the names of its lines, answering 'seen in the as-found photographs, not on the list: …' under Possible omissions. No line is written and nothing is ticked; the TC adds the item with + Add line item or answers 'not inventory'.
findings.decided_conflict: Decided: 'An Agent One sweep of the as-found shots (Anthony, 2026-09-30)'. This is a completeness flag, not naming, but it reads as-found photographs.
findings.vnote: The description is accurate: agentShotGroups and the room check read only Items photographs, so nothing compares the list with the as-found pass (code reading; the harm is reasoning). The proposal has an agent read as-found photographs, which is on the Decided list: 'An Agent One sweep of the as-found shots (Anthony, 2026-09-30: "agent one should only look [at] detailed inventory photos, not as-found")'. It is flag-only, but it is still an as-found read. The auditor flagged this correctly. It is worth putting to Anthony as a completeness question for estates.
findings.vrepro: CLAUDE.md, Decided: do not re-propose (as-found sweep); havellin.html agentShotGroups / agentRoomsToCheck (_arCheckable: Items lines only)

findings.title: On living work Agent Two researches Keep and New-home lines and flags their values 'unsure' though no client paper prints them
findings.where: agentValueAuto values every photographed named line whatever its disposition (havellin.html:38873); invLineUnsure exempts only agentValueInternal (counsel values) (37245); the Contents Record prints no values (manual).
findings.evidence: Code reading; s6 (a living Home Transition): 'Unsure 8' of 13 lines after the automatic run, with values on Keep and Move lines included.
findings.tc_impact: TC: research minutes and unsure flags on the client's own sofa moving to the new home, where the figure is not needed for any paper or decision.
findings.proposal: On living work, value Undecided and leaving lines (Sell, Consign, Auction, Donate, Distribute) automatically, and value a line when it moves to one of those; Keep, Move and Junk only on Value N lines. Show unsure for a living figure only on a selling line or one whose range reaches the specialist threshold.
findings.decided_conflict: AGENT_TWO_SPEC / havellin.html P23 decision 2: 'EVERY LINE, on every job that keeps an inventory, estates and living clients alike'.
findings.vnote: agentValueAuto values every named, photographed line whatever its disposition (havellin.html:38873). invLineUnsure exempts only agentValueInternal. The living Contents Record prints net proceeds, not FMV (printContentsRecord, 35600-35610). The proposal contradicts P23 decision 2, 'EVERY LINE, on every job that keeps an inventory, estates and living clients alike' (havellin.html:38415). The auditor flagged it.

findings.title: The Evening Desk says nothing of Agent Two's notes, or that a tick made before Agent Two finishes comes back unreviewed
findings.where: evening-desk-guide.html, '3. Tonight's items'; concierge-guide.html mentions 'Agent Two noted N lines to look at' only.
findings.evidence: grep -c 'noted|Appraisal advised|Worth a specialist' evening-desk-guide.html → 0. The page orders 'The values follow by themselves' before 'One Reviewed tick covers it all; press Unsure first', with no word to wait for 'Agent Two: N valued'. s2 shows early ticks undone; s3 shows Agent Two's notes are the tallest block above the rows (610 px).
findings.tc_impact: TC: the desk's largest list goes unexplained, and following the page's order loses the first ticks of the evening.
findings.proposal: Add, under the values sentence: 'Agent Two's notes (Appraisal advised, Worth a specialist, Look at this) sit under Agent Two noted N items; a tick takes the note off. Start ticking once the Inventory Review bar says Agent Two: N valued; an item ticked before its value lands comes back for one more look.' Hold both sentences in tests/evening-desk-guide.test.js.
findings.vnote: grep -c -E 'noted|Appraisal advised|Worth a specialist' evening-desk-guide.html → 0. The page explains Agent One's notes (line 408) but never the 'Agent Two noted N lines' list. It says 'The values follow by themselves' and 'One Reviewed tick covers it all; press Unsure first', with no word about waiting for the values. One correction: line 425 does say 'A name you typed with a destination chosen counts as reviewed until Agent Two values it', which covers a typed name being reopened, though not a ticked line.
